subject: dogs
one_liner: Rollover deploys your dog to the edge of the yard and reverts it to its last known good state (asleep) the moment the couch is at risk.
brand_voice_notes: Vercel press-release cadence applied to a dog. Every sentence is infrastructure-first, dog-second. Never acknowledges the joke: 'asleep' is a deployment state, the couch is a stakeholder, the mailman is an incident. Numbers are specific and slightly too confident (38ms rollbacks, 119 kennels of presence). No exclamation points; confidence is expressed through latency figures.

hero.sub: Rollover is zero-config dog infrastructure. Every walk gets a preview environment, every behavior ships behind a flag, and when the couch is at risk we revert your dog to its last known good state: asleep. Rollbacks land in 38 milliseconds, which is faster than remorse.

features.title: Preview Walks
features.blurb: Every behavioral change gets an isolated preview walk before it merges to the main route. Stakeholders (the neighbors, one squirrel) can comment directly on the walk. Nothing reaches your living room until it has been approved by at least one reviewer who is also a dog.

features.title: Instant Rollover
features.blurb: One click reverts your dog to the last deployment that did not involve the trash. Mid-zoomies, mid-bark, mid-shoe: state restores to asleep-on-the-cold-tile with zero downtime and no memory of the incident, on either side.

features.title: The Edge (of the Yard)
features.blurb: Your dog is replicated across 119 kennels of presence worldwide, so there is always a dog within 40 milliseconds of your hand. Fetch requests route to the nearest available dog. Cold starts apply to senior dogs only, and we think that's fair.

demo_screen_concept: The Rollover deployments dashboard for a production dog named Biscuit: header with the dog's domain (biscuit.dog) and a live READY status pill; a deployments table of recent behavior ships ('feat: bark at mailman', 'fix: stop eating couch', 'chore: relocate nap to sunbeam') each with build status, fake commit hash, preview-walk link and age; a working Instant Rollover button that reverts production to 'asleep (v112)' and prepends a rollback row; a live Bark Logs console streaming fake log lines; and an Edge Kennels panel listing per-region dog replicas with latency figures. Filter tabs (All / Ready / Error / Asleep) actually filter the table.

design_direction.style: Neo-brutalist municipal kennel-permit office crossed with a developer-tools launch page, daylight paper mode. The page is staged as the marketing site of a heavily funded frontend-infrastructure company that has decided the household dog is an availability problem and prices obedience by the millisecond. A warm form-stock cream ground carries flat panels with square-ish 10px radii, thick 2.5px ink borders, and hard offset shadows (6px right/down, solid ink, zero blur) so every card sits on the page like a laminated permit stapled to a corkboard. Depth comes entirely from border weight and shadow offset: no gradients as color, no blur, no glass, no clay, no hairline minimalism. Sticker chrome does the annotation: small bordered badges rotated 1 to 3 degrees (APPROVED, LICENSE NO. K9-2026, ZERO CONFIG) sit on card corners like inspection stickers, and a full-width bordered ticker strip scrolls recent deploy events between sections like a lost-dog notice board with a CI feed. One kennel cobalt carries the wordmark, section headings' underline slabs, primary buttons, and link states, applied as flat confident fill; one rationed fire-hydrant red is reserved strictly for the Instant Rollover motif, error states, the live status dot, and one sticker per screen, and appears nowhere else. Bricolage Grotesque sets the wordmark and headlines in wide chunky grotesque with the confidence of a company that laminates things; Instrument Sans carries plain, faintly procedural body copy. Every figure that pretends to be deployment telemetry (rollback latency, kennel counts, tail uptime, tier prices, commit hashes) is set in Martian Mono with tabular figures inside bordered wells, so it reads like a build log filled out in triplicate. Motion is stapler-blunt: cards translate up 2px and their shadow grows 2px on hover, buttons flatten to zero offset on press like a stamp, the status dot pulses on a 3s cycle, the deploy ticker scrolls linearly and pauses on hover, sections fade up 6px on scroll with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no terminal aesthetics, no monospace headlines, no glass, no blur, no clay, no bento lattice, no serifs, no postal motifs, no engraving. Reads like a company that files a dog's personality under 'workload' and considers the mailman a recurring incident with a known fix.

design_direction.motion_vocab: Hover: card lifts 2px, shadow grows. Press: button flattens to zero offset like a rubber stamp. Status dot 3s pulse. Linear marquee deploy ticker, pauses on hover. Sections fade up 6px, 40ms stagger. All behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Split hero: left column is the H1 with a cobalt underline slab, sub, and two buttons (cobalt primary, bordered ghost secondary); right column is a bordered 'deployment card' showing biscuit.dog with a READY pill, a fake commit list, and a big hydrant-red INSTANT ROLLOVER button, tilted 1.5deg with a hard shadow, an APPROVED sticker overlapping its corner. Deploy ticker strip runs full-width directly under the hero.
